skeptic.objection: This is not raw land. It is an operating Enterprise Holdings rental-car fleet facility. Fulton County Pretreatment Services shows an existing commercial waste discharge permit for Enterprise Holdings at 3600 Naturally Fresh Blvd, renewed on 7 Jan 2025. The county's tax year 2027 parcel record still carries improvements and a different owner, an out-of-state LLC, so the operator is almost certainly a tenant. Together with the 2005 purchase at $14.4M (from the brief; about four times today's appraised total), this reads as a leased investment property. It would be bought at income value, and it cannot be built on until the lease ends. The first pass flagged the site as occupied, but only from a 2003-2013 state contract sheet. This 2025 county record makes current operating use the main question. Zoning (M-1, South Fulton) and the Industrial plan designation hold up; the lead turns on the lease term and the owner's intentions, which only a person can find out.

The same record calls the facility an Enterprise Holdings site.

The county parcel layer, queried by parcel id, is already on tax year 2027 for this site address. It still lists the out-of-state LLC as owner, so the owner has not changed and is not the operator named on the 2025 permit.
Owner field of the same tax year 2027 county record (not Enterprise Holdings).

Despite the 'College Park' mailing address on the permit, the county's city-limits layer (Tax/Tyler_Cities), queried at the parcel's point (33.610533, -84.505301), puts the site in the City of South Fulton (tax code 55, consistent with the parcel's TaxDist 55H). The South Fulton zoning sources the first pass used are the right jurisdiction.

This supports the first pass on intent; it is still not the adopted use table.

The same 2026 staff report, written under the 2026 Comprehensive Plan, describes the Industrial land use category as dedicated to warehousing and distribution. The newer plan does not point the other way on the category itself. Whether this parcel keeps that designation on the 2026 map was not checked.

open_items: Lease: the parcel appears to be leased to Enterprise Holdings (operator on a 2025 county permit; owner is a separate out-of-state LLC; 2005 purchase at $14,375,000 per the brief, versus a 2027 appraised total of $3,447,300). A person should pull the recorded deed and any memorandum of lease from the Fulton County deed records to learn the lease term, renewal options and any tenant purchase option or right of first refusal, before treating this as a land lead.

If the lease runs for years, the lead is a future redevelopment play, not a land acquisition: the buyer would pay income value for a leased asset and inherit the tenant. The screener's land-value and seller-motivation scoring does not model this.

The 2025 permit concerns exterior subsurface tanks (fee tier 1-5) at a fleet facility. A Phase I environmental assessment should check for fuel storage tanks, vehicle wash and maintenance, and oil/water separators before any redevelopment.

The permit is from Fulton County Pretreatment Services, which suggests the site discharges to Fulton County sanitary sewer. Utilities stay unknown until the provider confirms; nothing quoted here says 'sewer'.

I checked the first pass's zoning-1 column alignment in the 2020 draft (page 39, layout text): the 'A' marks for Distribution Center and General Warehousing sit exactly under the M-1 and M-2 headers. The quote reads as claimed. It is still a draft; the adopted Appendix C Table 2-4 (Municode) was not read.

Overlay districts and any conditions from a past Fulton County rezoning of this parcel were not checked (the city zoning map is on ArcGIS Online, which cannot be fetched here). Note that the Z26-001 site sits in the Sandtown Overlay; ask planning whether any overlay covers Naturally Fresh Blvd.
